scope: Exact source/engine-input replay. Promotion clearance remains; two mating deflections and one actual-ply self-interference improve secondary explanations. All twenty-three primary IDs remain unchanged from adapter95, not certified accurate. Larger-ending and quiet-combination coverage gaps are retained.

motifs.label: Forcing Mate
motifs.evidence: Qxf7+ starts a forced mating attack. Every legal defence permits mate within 3 moves; one verified line is Qxf7+ Rxf7 Rd8+ Rf8 Rfxf8#. The exact continuation depends on the defence.

motifs.label: Checkmate
motifs.evidence: Rfxf8# is checkmate: the king is in check and there is no legal reply.

motifs.label: Mating Deflection
motifs.evidence: Qxf7+ offers the queen to deflect the rook from f8. Accepting with Rxf7 allows a verified mate starting with Rd8+ (Rf8 Rfxf8#): the defender no longer guards d8. The other legal replies also allow immediate mate; for example, Kh8 Qxf8#. Every legal defence permits mate. This is the supporting mechanism, not an extra material win.

Every legal defence is separately mated; clearance explains this branch, not a compulsory reply or an extra material win.

timeline.label: Forcing Mate

timeline.label: Mating Deflection
timeline.evidence: R1e6+ draws the king away from defending g7. After Kg5, Rxg7# is checkmate. Capturing on g7 first would allow the king to take that piece. Every legal reply allows this mating capture; this is the mechanism at this move, not a separate material win.

timeline.label: Self-Interference
timeline.evidence: Kg5 blocks Black's rook on g4 from defending the pawn on g7. Rxg7# is now checkmate; the guard's line was open before this move. On the resulting mating board, this blocker is the only obstruction to a king-safe recapture. This explains the concession, not a tactic won by Black.
